newsitem.title: UK: LVMH sees extra 65 mln stg merger savings.
newsitem.headline: LVMH sees extra 65 mln stg merger savings.

text.p: LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton said on Thursday a three-way drinks merger with itself and partners Grand Metropolitan and Guinness Plc would lead to additional cost savings of 65 million stg over and above what the two British groups had identified in their merger proposal.
LVMH chairman Bernard Arnault is expected to zero in on these estimated extra savings when he meets institutional investors in London on Thursday.
Guinness and Grandmet had said that merger of the two companies would result in annual cost savings of 175 million stg.

Luxury goods maker LVMH, the largest shareholder in both Guinness and Grandmet, has opposed the merger due to what analysts say is feared risks of marginalising its Moet Hennessy drinks business and locking up part of the group's capital in a subsidiary of the merged group.

LVMH said its extra savings would come from closer integration of the existing joint ventures between Moet Hennessy and Guinness' United Distillers (UD) with other distribution companies of UD and those of International Distillers & Vintners, a division of Grandmet.

"Further, LVMH estimates that at least as much additional annual operating profit will arise from placing Moet Hennessy's upper premium brands under common ownership with those of UD and IDV and marketing them together," the French group said.
LVMH, which currently holds 11.05 percent in Grandmet and 12.5 percent in Guinness, is proposing merging its Moet Hennessy cognac and champagne business with the UD and IDV.
The proposal could create a global drinks group of 7.4 billion stg with market leadership in five out six premium drinks categories.
"LVMH remains convinced that its proposal creates maximum value for all shareholders," it said.
